_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.vcs.vcs` is a semio-NATIVE checkpoint document — its wire forms are `.vcs.dsl.semio` and `.vcs.pack.semio`, both defined by this repository alone — so no oracle is registered and the evidence rests on the committed per-kind specification vectors plus the inverse law (see noOracleDecisions).

noOracleDecisions.rationale: There is no third-party implementation of `s.vcs.vcs` to compare against. The artifact is a review-checkpoint document invented here — title, an integer counter, freeform notes, a workflow status word and an ORDERED tag list — and its two wire forms (`🚪️io/📸️snapshot/📝️text`'s `.vcs.dsl.semio` and `💾️binary`'s `.vcs.pack.semio`) are grammars this repository defines and nobody else reads. Registering a general JSON or key-value library would not adjudicate a single one of the six kinds: what is under test is not how `{"tag": "urgent"}` serializes but that AddTag APPENDS after the members the base already carried, that a duplicate add degrades to `mutation.no-op` with an EMPTY inverse, and that RemoveTag against an absent tag is `mutation.target-missing` rather than a silent success — semantics no external package can hold an opinion about. Confidence comes instead from the six committed, independently handcrafted `(before, mutation, after, diff, outcome)` specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<slug>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, each already unit-tested inside the production crate itself, re-exercised end to end here through `apply_vcs_mutation_reporting`; and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property, asserted in role by the subject handler rather than inferred from an oracle's silence. Note that this catalog declares NO `no-mutation` and NO `set-snapshot`: whole-document replace is banned vocabulary in this taxonomy and reaches the store through its non-history `reset` path, so the two kinds every 🗄️stdio catalog carries genuinely do not exist here.
